title: Recording solos he liked best
summary: He recalls the nervousness of studio dates and names solos he liked, including Manteca, the Buck Clayton and Frankie Laine session and lost sides with Trummy Young.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: They always want you to be on time, then you get there and you never knew what was going to happen. You wrote the music and you wonder, you know, if you would be able to play the music and then if you had a solo, naturally you were concerned about your solo. Well, the Manteca solo I enjoyed very much doing and then the things I did with Buck Clayton, Frankie Lane on Columbia. I liked those solos. And some solos I did with J.C. Heard on RCA Victor with Etta Jones, I liked some of those things and then those things I did with Trummy Young. Those records were lost; I don't know where they're at, but I liked what I did on those.
